note: Authoritative local data from L1 chains.db (DeFiLlama + CoinGecko + growthepie/Dune). Raw signals, no scores. null = NO DATA (do not guess). FRESHNESS: price & market caps are live (today); TVL/stablecoin LEVELS are the latest available (carried forward if a chain's today-point isn't in yet); daily-FLOW metrics (DEX volume, fees, active_addresses, tx_count) are the LAST COMPLETE UTC DAY (today is partial and excluded) — full-day figures, use them as-is. SHARES are each chain's % of the WHOLE DeFi market (all ~500 chains; denominators in market.total_*), so tracked chains sum to <100% and deltas are immune to which chains we track. TVL/volume are USD-denominated, so share moves in a big market swing partly reflect token price, not pure flows. Each chain ALSO carries its OWN raw TVL growth — tvl_change_1d/7d/30d_pct (chain's level vs itself N days ago); use THESE for 'is this chain's TVL growing', NOT the share deltas (share = slice of market, a different question). If tvl_suspect_1d is true the 1d move is a likely upstream data glitch (a >25% one-day swing) — discount the 1d figure and lean on the 7d/30d trend instead. Stablecoins mirror this: stable_change_1d/7d/30d_pct are the chain's OWN stablecoin-supply trend (use for 'is stablecoin capital arriving/leaving', and to confirm or debunk 'stables doubled/halved' claims); stable_suspect_1d flags a >30% one-day swing as a likely DeFiLlama adapter flap (a bridged asset dropping in/out of the index) — call it out as a data-quality event, not a capital flow, and lean on 7d/30d. N-days-ago baselines are median-smoothed, so a one-day glitch can't fake a 7d/30d trend.

emerging_candidates.how_to_use: RAW watchlist of non-radar chains rising on the signals below — NOT buy calls. A candidate becomes a LEAD only on confluence (also trending / in a heating narrative / has a catalyst / fresh dev-gov) or a confirmed on-chain TVL surge.

signal_glossary.volume_heat: Volume is large vs market cap (turnover ≥15%) — unusual interest building.
signal_glossary.vol_leads_price: Volume is hot but 7d price hasn't run yet — interest building BEFORE the move (the early sweet spot).
signal_glossary.momentum: 7d gain keeping pace with / exceeding 30d — the move is accelerating, not fading.
signal_glossary.low_float: Only a small share of supply circulates — CAUTION: unlock overhang can cap upside.
signal_glossary.tvl_surge: On-chain TVL jumped ≥25% in 7d from a small base — real capital arriving, not just token price.

pre_winner_lookalikes.method: validated winner-DNA coil screen (deep-below-high + oversold + at-30d-low [all validated, hold OOS] + below-ATH/high-vol/mid-float/small-cap); primed-but-not-yet-moved. NECESSARY-not-sufficient setup — needs an event trigger.
pre_winner_lookalikes.how_to_use: Beaten-down coils matching the data-validated winner DNA. SETUPS, not buys: most never move. Edge comes ONLY from confluence — a lookalike that is also trending / in a heating narrative / has a near catalyst / has fresh dev-gov.

signal_glossary.deep_below_60d_high: Trading <50% of its 60-day high — deeply beaten down. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.oversold_30d: Down >25% over 30 days — oversold. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample).
signal_glossary.at_30d_low: Trading within ~3% of its 30-day low RIGHT NOW — the capitulation launch zone. VALIDATED (held out-of-sample); a bounce off the low actually LOWERS winner odds, so this is a timing edge.
signal_glossary.oversold_90d: Down >40% over 90 days — sustained downtrend (supporting context).
signal_glossary.deep_below_ath: Trading <15% of all-time high — far from prior peak, room to recover.
signal_glossary.high_vol: Elevated 30d volatility — capable of large moves.
signal_glossary.mid_float: Meaningful but not-fully-diluted float — the winner sweet spot.
signal_glossary.small_cap: Sub-$100M market cap — small enough to multiply.

Each item carries release_notes / body (truncated) + a keyword dimension_hint (raw, NOT a verdict) — the FOLLOW-UP is to read these and judge what the change actually does and whether it improves the protocol at a fundamental level (consensus/scaling/security/economics/new capability) vs routine housekeeping. No composite score.

dev.release_notes: Hotfix release. Binaries are pre-built and attached as assets. Source for this release is not published in this repository.

**v6.6.2** is a patch release focused on RPC and node-serving stability. The most impactful changes are the RPC-side fixes: the inbound P2P accept rate is now configurable with a higher default (#3939), and the state store DB layer honors context cancellation so abandoned queries no longer keep doing work (#3957). 

**Upgrade guidance:** recommended for RPC and full-node operators. **Optional for validators** — there are no state-machine or consensus-affecting changes, so validators can upgrade at their convenience.

## Overview

> [!NOTE]
> This is a patch release of op-supernode containing bug fixes and improved observability. It is an optional but recommended upgrade for interop operators.

Note: the Lagoon (interop) hardfork is not yet live in production. Changes to those code paths in this release are preparation for future functionality and do not affect operators today.

## What's Changed

### Bug fixes

- A chain could stay frozen after an invalidation and needed a supernode restart to recover. This was a rare corner case, reached only when the invalidation completed without a rewind (#22370)
- `op_node_supernode_info` reported a hardcoded version of `0.1.0` rather than the version built into the binary. If you alert or dashboard on this series, expect the value to change after upgrading (#22104)

### Observability

- Chain rewinds now record duration and failure metrics, and log with more context (#22088)
- New Prometheus counters `FollowSourceReorgs` and `SuperAuthorityReorgSignals` record follow-source and SuperAuthority reorg decisions in the virtual nodes (#22106)

### Other

- Gas estimation now lets the target node apply its own fork rules instead of pinning a fixed ceiling. Behaviour on Karst/Osaka is unchanged; EIP-8037-aware nodes can now use the block limit (#22217)
- Internal refactoring of shared L2 client and receipt handling, with no operator-facing change (#21908, #22295)

### Lagoon (not yet in production)

- Adjusted PostExec payload …[truncated]

  * **Recommended:** Download a new snapshot `base-reth-node download`. See the [docs](https://docs.base.org/base-chain/node-operators/snapshots) for more information.
  * Migrate your existing V1 data `base-reth-node db migrate-v2`. Note: `migrate-v2` is expected to take **much** longer than `download`. Non-archival nodes are not supported for this command.
- **Upgrades Reth to v2.3.0**
- Bug fixes and stability improvements

### base-consensus
- **Fixed prune node sync**: Nodes can reliably do a pruned node sync from genesis
- Bug fixes and stability improvements

governance.body:
# Arbitrum Security Program

## Abstract

The Arbitrum Foundation proposes to continue and evolve the Arbitrum Audit Program (AAP) - [launched on 1 August 2025](https://blog.arbitrum.foundation/arbitrums-10m-audit-program-is-live-apply-to-secure-your-smart-contracts/) with a one-year mandate - into a broader Arbitrum Security Program (ASP), running for a further 12 months on a rolling-application basis.

- **From "Audit" to "Security".** AAP delivered on its original purpose - real vulnerabilities surfaced and remediated before mainnet, with a high share of net-new teams brought to Arbitrum - and demonstrated where subsidised security converts into the most ecosystem value. Building on that, the mandate broadens to four pillars covering the full security lifecycle: AI-assisted screening ahead of a full audit, the human-conducted audit itself, the Arbitrum bug bounty program, and the ArbitrumDAO Security Council.

- **No new treasury request.** ~$2M in cumulative audit commitments is expected by AAP's close. The remaining $1.76M USDC + 25M ARB held by the Foundation becomes ASP's operational budget, less ~$1.2M in predicted outstanding deployments.
